Ruled: **A** — only the paired `<base>.custom` declares an override; rider 3 of 6540351677 ("any package in the closure may declare") is withdrawn.

Maintainer, verbatim, in the desktop PM session, replying 「同意」 to the seat's business explanation that recommended A (partner packages only **add** items under their own names; the customer's `.custom` is the one layer that changes a base item; owner fixed by role, not by publish order). Freshness gate: thread had 0 comments at recording; body unedited since filing.

**What this card now carries (execution card, `pm:queue`, lane `domain:skills`):** one ADR amendment PR to `docs/adr/0146-studio-designs-setup-administers-one-editor-per-item-paired-customize-package.md` (Tier H — maintainer merges), applying the "裁 A" list in this card's body verbatim in intent:
- D2: delete the partner sentence (:188–189); the declaring item is "an item of the base's paired `.custom` package" (:191–192); the closure paragraph (:212–214) becomes — a dependent's same-named item has one fix, rename; a dependent that carries `overrides` is refused at publish, at `os validate` and at the install door; "the refusal names both fixes" holds for `.custom` only.
- D8.2 (:408) "the `.custom` item that declares it"; D9.1 (:433–434) "from `.custom`".
- Supersede table (:524 / :526 / :530), Q1 row (:553), Consequences (:580), N-09 row (:603) narrowed to match.
- ADR-0048 :3 and ADR-0126 :3 pointer lines: drop "or the declared override a package in its dependency closure publishes" / "(or in a dependent package that declares it)".
- Cost on record: a partner that wants a different base view ships it under its own name; if a real partner need to replace a base item appears later, it reopens as option B with that evidence.

Line numbers are readings of main at filing; the PR re-reads them. PR body: `Fixes #28390`, `## 维护者速读(草稿)` per the governed-surface rule.

**Effect on the N-09 riders** (#28236 comment 6541767586): under A the Supersede-table residue and the D2-heading residue become true as written and need no edit; gap 1's install-door check reduces to "a dependent artifact carries no `overrides` and no base item's name". N-09 carries `Blocked-by: #28390` and implements A.

1. D9's action paragraph: an undeclared same-name `action` in a dependent is refused like any other kind; until action override opens, the only fix is rename.
2. D9's tense: the action ledger switch is no longer pending — #27842 and #27504 closed on 2026-10-30.

ADR-0146's cost list (Consequences) gains gap 3: a base upgrade that adds a name a `.custom` item already holds displaces that item (D8 item 2) — no door judges a base upgrade (ADR-0141 D3 deferred); N-09 makes the install/upgrade door name each collision, N-10 surfaces the orphan in the layered read.
Source: N-09 riders on the epic (6541767586 item 3 and item 2(b), amended by 6542181562). The Supersede-table and D2-heading residues need no edit under A.

Notify: scope · #28390 · one more ADR-0146 text item, from the N-08 ruling

The maintainer's ruling on PR #28467 (recorded on #28404 as 6549129352: 田騏, verbatim 「同意」, 2026-10-31 20:44Z) carries follow-up (c): `basedOn` records the **base package's `manifest.version`** the override was taken from, not a history version of the item; "the ADR-0146 D2 wording is to be aligned in the #28390 text amendment". PR #28467 already changed the schema's `.describe()` to this meaning.

Added to this card's amendment, beside the items in 6543281223. Lines read on `origin/main` today:
- D2 L195: `basedOn: '<the base item's version the override was taken from>'` → the base package's `manifest.version`.
- D2 L201: "`basedOn` records which version of the base's item the author started from" → which version of the base package.
- Migration paragraph L499: "`basedOn` set to the base item's version at migration" → the installed base package's version at migration.
- L282, L571 and L644–646 talk about `basedOn` being recorded and read by a human, and need no change of meaning. Re-read them when editing, in case a sentence there says "item version".

Nothing else changes: `basedOn` stays recorded and never judged, which is the epic's *Not in this epic* line.
